studies.Population: Men aged 40–79 years participating in the Miyagi and Ohsaki cohort studies
studies.Reference: Mushroom consumption and incident risk of prostate cancer in Japan: A pooled analysis of the Miyagi Cohort Study and the Ohsaki Cohort Study.
studies.Authors: Zhang S, Sugawara Y, Chen S, Beelman RB, Tsuduki T, Tomata Y, Matsuyama S, Tsuji I
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Data on mushroom consumption (categorized as <1, 1-2 and ≥3 times/week) was collected using a validated food frequency questionnaire.

sample_size.excerpt: In the present study, a total of 36,499 men, aged 40-79 years, who participated in the Miyagi Cohort Study in 1990 and in the Ohsaki Cohort Study in 1994 were followed for a median of 13.2 years.

cases.excerpt: During 574,397 person-years of follow-up, 1,204 (3.3%) cases of prostate cancer were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared to participants with mushroom consumption <1 time/week, frequent mushroom intake was associated with a decreased risk of prostate cancer (1-2 times/week: HRs [95% CIs] = 0.92 [0.81, 1.05]; ≥3 times/week: HRs [95% CIs] = 0.83 [0.70, 0.98]; p-trend = 0.023).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared to participants with mushroom consumption <1 time/week, frequent mushroom intake was associated with a decreased risk of prostate cancer (1-2 times/week: HRs [95% CIs] = 0.92 [0.81, 1.05]; ≥3 times/week: HRs [95% CIs] = 0.83 [0.70, 0.98]; p-trend = 0.023).

comparison.excerpt: Compared to participants with mushroom consumption <1 time/week, frequent mushroom intake was associated with a decreased risk of prostate cancer

studies.Title: Vegetable and fruit consumption and prostate cancer risk: a cohort study in The Netherlands.
studies.Reference: Vegetable and fruit consumption and prostate cancer risk: a cohort study in The Netherlands.
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.Population: men aged 55-69 years at baseline in 1986
studies.comparison_type: per increment of 25 g/day of mushroom consumption

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: The association between 21 vegetables and eight fruits and prostate cancer risk was assessed in the Netherlands Cohort Study among 58,279 men of ages 55-69 years at baseline in 1986. After 6.3 years of follow-up, 610 cases with complete vegetable data and 642 cases with complete fruit data were available for analysis.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: After 6.3 years of follow-up, 610 cases with complete vegetable data and 642 cases with complete fruit data were available for analysis.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Observed positive associations were significant for consumption of leek (RR, 1.38) and oranges (RR, 1.07) and nonsignificant for sweet peppers (RR, 1.60) and mushrooms (RR, 1.49). Results in subgroups of cases were more or less consistent with the overall results.
extraction_supporting_text.continent: a cohort study in The Netherlands
extraction_supporting_text.location: Vegetable and fruit consumption and prostate cancer risk: a cohort study in The Netherlands
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: Individual vegetables and fruits were evaluated as continuous variables (g/day)
